Bachelor in Applied Sciences and Masters in Computer Applications Brief profile and experience N Chandrasekaran is the Chairman of Tata Sons, the holding company and promoter of all Tata group companies. He joined the Board of Tata Sons in October 2016 and was appointed Chairman in January 2017.

He also chairs the Boards of several group operating companies, including Tata Steel, Tata Motors, Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles, Tata Power, Air India, Tata Consumer Products, Indian Hotels Company and TCS.

Before becoming the Chairman, he was the Chief Executive Officer (“CEO”) of TCS, a company in which he served 30 years, including eight, until 2017, as its CEO. Under his leadership, TCS became the country's most valuable company.

Before becoming the Chairman, he was the Chief Executive Officer (“CEO”) of TCS, a company in which he served 30 years, including eight, until 2017, as its CEO. Under his leadership, TCS became the country's most valuable company.

At the Tata group, he has pursued the “One Tata” strategy, based on the themes of simplification, scale and synergy. Now he is driving transformation of the Tata group towards a sustainable future. He has steered the group into new businesses including semiconductors, electronics manufacturing, consumer internet platform, mobile technology and battery gigafactories. The Tata group has expanded its aviation presence with the acquisition of Air India and is building a large global airline. The group's turnover exceeded US$180 Billion with a market cap of US$328 Billion as on March 31, 2025.

N Chandrasekaran is on the International Advisory Council of Singapore's Economic Development Board, Mitsubishi's International Advisory Committee and on the Board of Governors of New York Academy of Sciences. He is the Co-Chair of the India US CEO Forum.

The numerous recognitions conferred on him include, the Padma Bhushan, one of India's highest civilian awards in 2022 and France' highest civilian award Légion d'Honneur, in 2023. In 2025, he was conferred Honorary Knight of the Most Excellent Order of the British Empire.

He has been awarded several honorary doctorates by leading Universities in India and internationally, including an honorary Doctor of Letters from Macquarie University, Australia, Doctor Honoris Causa by Nyenrode University, The Netherlands, and Doctor of Letters from the Regional Engineering College, Trichy, Tamil Nadu.

N Chandrasekaran is also the author of Bridgital Nation, a groundbreaking book on harnessing technological disruptions to bring Indians closer to their dreams.

He is an avid photographer, and a passionate long-distance marathon runner. He is a Six Star Finisher of the World Marathon Majors and continues to champion fitness.

Adaptive AI is a type of artificial intelligence that continuously learns and updates its models in realtime, based on new data and user feedback, to adapt to changing environments without needing to be fully retrained.

Agentic AI is an advanced form of artificial intelligence focused on autonomous decision-making and action. Unlike traditional AI, which primarily responds to commands or analyzes data, agentic AI can set goals, plan, and execute tasks with minimal human intervention.

An agentic enterprise is a business that uses autonomous AI agents to reason, make decisions, and execute multi-step workflows, shifting AI usage from passive chatbots to active partners. These agents are goal-driven, adaptable, and integrated, handling routine operations to allow human employees to focus on high-value, strategic work.

An AI agent is a software program that acts autonomously to achieve specific goals by perceiving its environment, reasoning, planning, and using tools.

Systematic and unfair discrimination in AI outputs arising from biased training data, flawed model architecture, or skewed feedback loops.

A data centre designed to host AI workloads and the required compute, cooling, power, storage, and networking capabilities.

The broader network of talent, partnerships, platforms, infrastructure, and solutions required to develop and deploy AI at scale.

The broader network of talent, partnerships, platforms, infrastructure, and solutions required to develop and deploy AI at scale.

An Al ecosystem orchestration partner is a strategic service provider that manages the complex integration of various Al technologies-including multiple models, infrastructure, data sources, and autonomous agents to create a unified and scalable business system to deliver end-to-end impact.

AI engineering is foundational for enterprise delivery of AI solutions at scale. The discipline unifies DataOps, MLOps and DevOps pipelines to create coherent enterprise development, delivery (hybrid, multicloud, edge), and operational (streaming, batch) AI-based systems.

A structured environment that enables organizations to build, deploy, and scale AI solutions efficiently.

It brings together data, computing infrastructure, AI models, tools, and governance to convert data into actionable intelligence at scale.

The policies, processes, standards, and oversight mechanisms organisations use to manage the lifecycle, risks, and ethical implications of AI systems.

AI guardrails are safety rules, filters, and mechanisms that ensure AI systems, particularly LLMs and chatbots, operate safely, ethically, and accurately. They function as protective boundaries, monitoring inputs and outputs to prevent harmful content, data breaches, hallucinations, and bias, thereby ensuring responsible and reliable AI performance.

The use of a trained AI model to generate outputs, predictions, or responses from new prompts or inputs.

AIOps (Artificial Intelligence for IT Operations) combines big data and machine learning to automate IT operations processes, including event correlation, anomaly detection and causality determination.

An AI platform is a comprehensive software framework or unified environment that provides tools, infrastructure, and services to develop, train, deploy, and manage machine learning and AI applications.

A structured evaluation of an organisation's data assets, infrastructure, talent, and governance maturity to determine its readiness for AI adoption.

A reference design or deployment model for building data centre infrastructure suited to AI workloads.

Infrastructure designed to support AI workloads with the required performance, resilience, connectivity, and efficiency.

The process of developing and training an AI model using data to learn patterns and improve performance.

A computing workload related to AI model training, inferencing, fine-tuning, or running AI models and applications.

Stakeholder Engagement and Identification of Material Topics Sustainability is embedded at the core of our decision-making, guiding how we create long-term value for stakeholders. Through structured engagement and robust assessment, we continuously refine our focus on the most material ESG priorities.

TCS follows a structured and comprehensive approach to identify ESG issues that are most material to its business. This process is anchored in two key pillars: (i) continuous engagement with a diverse set of stakeholders, and (ii) a systematic evaluation of evolving industry trends and market dynamics. This enables TCS to align its business objectives with stakeholder expectations while supporting long-term sustainable growth.

To ensure relevance and accuracy, TCS conducts periodic materiality assessments using a well-defined and sequential methodology:

Engagement with stakeholders Engagement across stakeholder groups provides insights into varied expectations and priorities. These inputs are gathered through both internal and external interactions and are carefully analyzed and prioritized to identify material topics that have significant economic, environmental, social, and governance impacts on TCS' operations and performance.

Sustainability context and value chain TCS evaluates its role within the broader sustainability ecosystem by assessing both direct and indirect impacts of its operations, client engagements, and industry participation. This holistic perspective ensures that stakeholder concerns are addressed not only at an operational level but also within the larger value chain and business ecosystem.
